1.explanation:
• index.md describes which file extensions map to the built-in TypeScript parser (so you can verify .mts is recognized as TS).  
• options.md explains the `trailingComma` setting that governs insertion/removal of commas in parameters and generics.  
• configuration.md shows how to customize or override parser settings (for example to force `--parser typescript` or set `trailingComma` differently for .mts).  
• cli.md documents how Prettier picks parsers based on file extension or user‐supplied `--parser`, relevant if .mts isn’t auto‐recognized.  
• technical-details.md dives into how Prettier’s TypeScript parser handles AST nodes for type parameters, which is where the comma is lost.  
• plugins.md covers how to add or override language support (in case fixing .mts handling requires a plugin approach). These files together allow you to trace how .mts files are detected, parsed, and formatted with respect to generic argument commas and to reproduce or patch the behavior.
1.bug_scenario: In a .mts module, when formatting an unconstrained generic function signature such as “export const unsafeCoerce = <T,>(u: unknown): T => u as T”, Prettier (v2.8.4) strips out the required trailing comma after “T”. The IDE then flags a TS7060 error (“This syntax is reserved in files with the .mts or .cts extension. Add a trailing comma or explicit constraint.”) because in .mts/.cts files an unconstrained type parameter list must end with a comma. The screenshot shows Prettier rendering “<T>” instead of “<T,>” and the TypeScript error overlay.
